=== THE NIL RETURN ON THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ, INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED ===
CBS's dedicated Iran live file, whose own URL slug includes "strait-of-hormuz", carries NO strike, NO interception and NO shipping incident in the Gulf or the Strait of Hormuz today. It carries NO updated oil price figure for today either.
Combined with the Al Jazeera Iran live blog (17:30 GMT) and the Times of Israel liveblog, that is THREE approved live files with nothing on Hormuz today. If you write a Hormuz line tonight, it can only be about the ABSENCE of an incident, or about Obama's "veto power" framing we already ran this morning. DO NOT IMPLY AN INCIDENT.

=== TRUMP — CBS HAS THE EARLIER POSITION, NOT THE LATER ONE ===
- CBS's most recent Trump comment is from SUNDAY MORNING: he is "weighing deal with Iran against action to 'finish them off'".
- VERBATIM, Donald Trump, President of the United States, speaking to FOX NEWS on Sunday: "Now, my question is, do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off?"
- SOURCING WARNING: FOX NEWS IS A BANNED SOURCE under our rules. CBS News, which is approved, is the source here, reporting what Trump said in a Fox interview. If you use the quote, attribute it to CBS News and say Trump said it in a television interview. DO NOT NAME FOX NEWS and do not link to it.
- IMPORTANT SEQUENCING: CBS at 17:22 GMT still had "deal or finish them off" as Trump's latest. The Times of Israel entry and the Al Jazeera live blog (dateModified 17:30 GMT) then carry the LATER and harder line, "There will not be a strike today." So tonight's movement is: Trump mused about a deal or finishing the job in the morning, and by late afternoon had ruled out a strike today. That sequence is the story, and it is the genuine advance on our 08:22 edition, which trailed a possible Sunday strike.

=== A NAMED IRANIAN OFFICIAL — NEW, AND WE HAVE NOTHING ELSE LIKE IT TONIGHT ===
- ABBAS ARAGHCHI, Foreign Minister of Iran, at a televised event on Sunday: "Whether there is war or not, our policies remain the same."
- TEHRAN'S ASSERTION. Label it. But it is a named foreign minister on the record, which is far better sourced than the unnamed "parliament speaker" quote on the Al Jazeera live blog.
- NAME-SPELLING CAUTION: CBS renders it "Abbas Araghchi". Check the spelling against a second approved source before printing if you can; do not silently correct it.
